conclusions.text: The broad retained fragment was already overwhelmingly uncovered in the complete 2017 native administrative products: their three-member union covers only the reported small fraction; Atlas reconciliation leaves the entire fragment uncovered. This supports that the broad seam predates Atlas reconciliation while showing that reconciliation removes a small source-covered portion.

Bilateral China–Tajikistan boundary agreements and an official 2010 demarcation protocol are documented, and Tajikistan MFA states delimitation/demarcation issues were resolved; the authoritative mapped line and its local position relative to this fragment remain unresolved because the protocol/maps were not acquired and matched.
Whether the entire retained polygon is dry land rather than river, seasonal water or another physical surface remains unresolved; the major-lakes-only non-hit cannot resolve that question.
The upstream metadata original-geometry digest recipe does not match the retrieved geometry under this packet’s canonical JSON serialization; the explanation remains unresolved.

Official bilateral records place the 2010 demarcation protocol and future joint-inspection coordinate records in the authority chain for marker location; the inspected 2012 agreement also expressly addresses seasonal boundary rivers and crossing waters. This identifies missing record types but does not locate the local line or classify the fragment.

The official demarcation map/coordinate record for this segment and its physical land/water status remain unresolved. The 2012 agreement refers to separate protocol/joint-inspection records not retrieved here; WorldCover 2021 v200 was reviewed only as an access-page lead, not analyzed.
